question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}x{y}^{3},\, & 0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

If $\text{E}[X]=\frac{2}{3}$ and $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{8}{5},$ find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ the covariance matrix $Σ$ is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}].
$$

Recall that the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}.
$$

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(\frac{1}{2}x{y}^{3})\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{3}\cdot {[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{1}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot {[\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 4 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-{(\frac{2}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we compute $\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}(\frac{1}{2}x{y}^{3})\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{5}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{5}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot {[\frac{1}{6}{y}^{6}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{32}{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}-{(\frac{8}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{75}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$ The joint support of $X$ and $Y$ is given by the rectangle

$$
S=[0,1]\times [0,2].
$$

Moreover, we can write

$$
f(x,y)=g(x)\cdot h(y),
$$

where $g(x)=2x$ and $h(y)=\frac{{y}^{3}}{4}.$

Hence, $X$ and $Y$ are independent, and consequently $\text{Cov}[X,Y]=0.$

Therefore, the covariance matrix is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{18} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{8}{75}\end{aligned}].
$$
